result.topic_en: Consequences of the trigonometric series φ/2 = sin φ − ½ sin 2φ + ⅓ sin 3φ − …: the case φ = 30°, its derivative and its successive integrals (giving π²/12 and π³/32), and a scholium resolving the apparent paradox at φ = π.
result.transcription:
168
4°. Sit $\phi = 30^\circ = \frac{\pi}{6}$, ac fit
$\frac{\pi}{12} = \frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \frac{1}{3} - \frac{1}{4}\cdot\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \frac{1}{5}\cdot\frac{1}{2} * - \frac{1}{7}\cdot\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{8}\cdot\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} - \text{etc.}$
feu
$\frac{\pi}{12} = \frac{1}{2}(1 + \frac{1}{5} - \frac{1}{7} - \frac{1}{11} + \frac{1}{13} + \frac{1}{17} - \frac{1}{19} - \frac{1}{23} + \text{etc.})$
$- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}(\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{8} - \frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{14} + \frac{1}{16} - \frac{1}{20} - \frac{1}{22} + \text{etc.})$
$+ \frac{1}{3}(1 - \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{5} - \frac{1}{7} + \frac{1}{9} - \frac{1}{11} + \text{etc.})$
quarum feriarum vltima fit $= \frac{\pi}{12}$, hinc concluditur
$1 + \frac{1}{5} - \frac{1}{7} - \frac{1}{11} + \frac{1}{13} + \frac{1}{17} - \text{etc.} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}(1 + \frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{5} + \frac{1}{7} + \frac{1}{8} - \text{etc.})$
Vtraque autem feries aequatur arcui $\frac{\pi}{3}$, quod quidem in priori ex Leibniziana eft manifeftum.
Corollarium 1.
§. 13. Ex aequatione hic inuenta:
$\frac{1}{2}\phi = \sin.\phi - \frac{1}{2}\sin.2\phi + \frac{1}{3}\sin.3\phi - \frac{1}{4}\sin.4\phi + \text{etc.}$
plures aliae non minus notatu dignae deriuari poffunt. Veluti inftituta differentiatione prodit
$\frac{1}{2} = \cos.\phi - \cos.2\phi + \cos.3\phi - \cos.4\phi + \text{etc.}$
cuius ratio inde eft manifefta, quod multiplicando vtrinque per $2\cos.\frac{1}{2}\phi$ prodit aequatio identica $\cos.\frac{1}{2}\phi = \cos.\frac{1}{2}\phi$.
Corollarium 2.
§. 14. At fi illam aequationem per $-d\phi$ multiplicatam integremus, prouenit
$C - \frac{1}{4}\phi\phi = \cos.\phi - \frac{1}{4}\cos.2\phi + \frac{1}{9}\cos.3\phi - \frac{1}{16}\cos.4\phi + \text{etc.}$
vbi ex cafu $\phi = 0$ conftans per integrationem ingreffa determinatur, fcilicet:
$C = 1 - \frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{9} - \frac{1}{16} + \text{etc.} = \frac{\pi\pi}{12}$,
ita

169
ita vt fit
$\frac{\pi\pi}{12} - \frac{\phi\phi}{4} = \cos.\phi - \frac{1}{4}\cos.2\phi + \frac{1}{9}\cos.3\phi - \frac{1}{16}\cos.4\phi + \text{etc.}$
quae ergo feries, fumto $\phi = \frac{\pi}{\sqrt{3}}$, fit $= 0$. Eft autem proxime
$\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{3}} = 103^\circ, 55', 23''$ et $\cos.\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{3}} = 0,240186$.
Corollarium 3.
§. 15. Si hanc aequationem denuo per $d\phi$ multiplicatam integremus, oritur haec noua fummatio:
$\frac{1}{12}\pi\pi\phi - \frac{1}{12}\phi^3 = \sin.\phi - \frac{1}{8}\sin.2\phi + \frac{1}{27}\sin.3\phi - \frac{1}{64}\sin.4\phi + \text{etc.}$
vnde fumto arcu $\phi = 90^\circ = \frac{\pi}{2}$ obtinetur
$\frac{1}{32}\pi^3 = 1 - \frac{1}{27} + \frac{1}{125} - \frac{1}{343} + \text{etc.}$
vti iam aliunde eft notum.
Scholion.
§. 16. Circa feriem inuentam
$\frac{1}{2}\phi = \sin.\phi - \frac{1}{2}\sin.2\phi + \frac{1}{3}\sin.3\phi - \text{etc.}$
dubium oriri poteft, quod fumto arcu $\phi = 180^\circ = \pi$, finguli feriei termini euanefcant, ideoque fumma nequeat ipfi $\frac{1}{2}\pi$ aequari. Verum ad hoc dubium foluendum ftatuatur primo $\phi = \pi - \omega$, et refultabit haec aequatio:
$\frac{\pi - \omega}{2} = \sin.\omega + \frac{1}{2}\sin.2\omega + \frac{1}{3}\sin.3\omega + \frac{1}{4}\sin.4\omega + \text{etc.}$
nunc vero arcus $\omega$ infinite paruus fumatur, vnde adipifcimur hanc:
$\frac{\pi - \omega}{2} = \omega + \omega + \omega + \omega + \omega + \text{etc.}$
quae nihil amplius continet abfurdi. Quod idem tenendum eft, fi velimus accipere $\phi = 2\pi$ vel $\phi = 3\pi$ etc.
Euleri Opusc. Anal. Tom. I. X Exem-

items.quote: Vtraque autem feries aequatur arcui $\frac{\pi}{3}$, quod quidem in priori ex Leibniziana eft manifeftum.
items.english: Each of the two series, moreover, equals the arc π/3, which is indeed evident for the first one from the Leibniz series.
This series therefore becomes 0 when φ = π/√3 is taken.
π³/32 = 1 − 1/27 + 1/125 − 1/343 + etc., as is already known from elsewhere.

items.quote: dubium oriri poteft, quod fumto arcu $\phi = 180^\circ = \pi$, finguli feriei termini euanefcant, ideoque fumma nequeat ipfi $\frac{1}{2}\pi$ aequari.
items.english: A doubt may arise, because when the arc φ = 180° = π is taken, every term of the series vanishes, so the sum cannot equal π/2.
